key_insight: An alternating-minimization control framework can synthesize high-fidelity multimode entangling gates in trapped-ion chains while suppressing residual motion and keeping control complexity manageable at large scale.
engineering_relevance: This suggests programmable, large-scale interaction engineering is feasible in trapped-ion processors using global or structured laser control rather than rapidly increasing hardware resources.
method: Directly searches for multi-tone control fields that realize target spin-spin couplings.
Alternates optimization steps to improve numerical stability in a high-dimensional non-convex problem.
Extends from global all-to-all and nearest-neighbor gates to individual addressing for structured qLDPC targets.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful synthesis of all-to-all and nearest-neighbor gates up to N = 1000 ions, and an individual-addressing qLDPC example at N = 512.
watch_item: The approach is numerical and may depend on model accuracy, optimization convergence, and experimentally achievable laser shaping under realistic noise and calibration limits.
paper_title: Large-scale multimode entangling-gate synthesis in trapped-ion systems
